title: The Power of the Cross
english: He remembers being named by men, from the very beginning of the contests of the name of Jesus Christ, from which all ought to be called. He does not complain about what is currently being said regarding dogmas, nor does he complain to them about this, but rather about what we have said before and what he demonstrates hereafter.

He asks: Are you not heirs with Christ, with whom he shared you, the believers? For he did not say, 'Christ was shared,' but rather, 'did Christ not share with you?' The argument demonstrates this, for he says: Was not Paul crucified for us? The Christ died for the salvation of the world, but none of us. From this, he shows that some intended to be named after the one who was baptizing them. This good thing, which the Savior also commanded and which brings salvation, became a burden to me, he says, if you were intending to be called from me, the one baptizing.

How then are we to understand that Christ did not send me to baptize, but to evangelize? Since even one who is not an apostle baptizes, yet the dignity of the apostles was held by few, and without being evangelized and being baptized, one could not be baptized, he says; I was sent to evangelize, for this is the preceding thing, not to baptize. It is therefore left here, by implication, that 'I was not previously sent to baptize.' Thus also elsewhere when he says: Does God not care for the oxen? Not because he does not care; for even in the Law, Moses says concerning oxen, truly concerning those who serve the farmers. And David says: Lord, you will save men and cattle, just as God has multiplied your mercy. And Solomon says: The righteous man has pity on the souls of his cattle, how much more God? But what is it that he says? That previously God does not care for the oxen. And here, by ellipsis, it is as if he said, 'that Christ did not send me to baptize.'

Moving to another fault and coming to another correction, not having completely set aside the first, he has used the second as a prelude. For the first was that Christ did not send me to baptize, regarding the fact that each of you says: 'I am of Paul,' or 'I am of Apollos'; the second is the word not in wisdom, the beginning of another administration. Thus, evangelizing has been set as the end of the first matter and the beginning of the second, so that the cross of Christ might not be emptied.

The proclamation declares that the power of the cross is not displayed. Concerning the word of the cross, it does not speak of the mere utterance or the sound, but of the power; for while the work appears to be weak, the cause, when sought, is revealed to be a great mystery. To us who are being saved, it is the power of God. Since Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God, and some desire to receive the word of God through Him, it must be observed that regarding the cross, the word speaks of the power of God.

For it is written: 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise.' Even though the apostle is himself credible in his teaching—for he had Christ speaking within himself—he has also made use of the testimony of the Old Testament, producing a more certain certainty for the disciples. Having used the testimony, 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise,' he proceeds as if upon what has already been agreed, saying: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? The wisdom of the Greeks, and the scribe of the Jews.

He mentions two wisdoms: one is the harmony observed in the created things, and the other is the wisdom according to which men, being rational, become intelligent. Since, he says, through the understanding coming to us we did not know God, nor through the wisdom observed in the created things, God was pleased to save those believing through the foolishness of the proclamation. Great is what he says, which is not shown to those passing by simply; for the power of God and all-wisdom demonstrates itself in this way.

The magnitude and the beauty of the world, he says, being immeasurable and ungraspable, did not persuade you to know God; rather, leaving the Maker, you worshipped these things through which it was necessary to know their Maker. God, showing the excess of His own power—whom creation did not persuade but even struck—enlightened the world through the agreed-upon weakness of the cross.

For showing the absurdity of those who have been emboldened in rationality and think to adorn piety through eloquence, he says that we must not answer not only those seeking wisdom among the Greeks, but also those Jews who ask for signs—the signs of the Spirit, and the wisdom of the words of external education. If they do not even ask for the wonders of the Spirit, it would have been fitting to give them the things of external wisdom—for not...

title: The Boasting of the Cross vs. Human Pride
english: They attempt to give, yet they ask in bad faith; the word is cast out entirely as one attacking the glory of the cross. But we preach Christ crucified and the following. It is evident that he says Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God according to the logic of the cross, as being superior; for the word of the cross is foolishness to those being destroyed, but to us being saved it is the power of God.

He demonstrates this more clearly after saying: to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, he brought Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God; because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men. Who would dare say the Word God is the weakness of God, and the foolishness of God regarding the crucified Christ? God the Word is powerful as the Father, not a power as a part fulfilling the essence of the Father, and likewise wise; since that which the visible creation, or angels, or archangels, or patriarchs, or prophets, or the law through Moses, or the voices from the midst of the fire brought to the people—which could not forgive the choice of the ungrateful—this, the foolishness of the cross, prevailed.

Therefore, Christ crucified is the power of God and the wisdom of God, more incomparable to all the economy and more reliable than all creation. And this is the power of the one who dispensed and perfected, having saved men through nothing and having brought them into faith in him.

Since the Jews test the Spirit of God, but it is to be granted to the believers, it is also necessary to answer the Greeks who think they can order piety by rationality; then he teaches how the preaching seems to be foolishness. For they seek signs and wisdom, but we preach Christ crucified, the power of God and the wisdom of God, and we promise salvation from the crucified one to those who believe.

It is not right to say the Word God is the weakness of God, but rather the cross of Christ; for the Word is powerful as the Father, not a power as a part fulfilling the essence of the Father. So also the Son is wise as the Father.

Not by angels, nor by law, nor by prophets, but because God forgives according to the choice of the ignorant, this thing which seems to be the foolishness of the cross has power. The crucified Christ is proclaimed as the power and wisdom of God, having been seen as stronger and more enduring, having saved those who believe. 1 Cor 1:26 The fleshly element was added, opposing the spirit, and the following things similarly give out according to the common. 1 Cor 1:29 So that no flesh may boast before Him; that is, so that the achievement of the preaching is not written upon the advantages of those at home. But he said 'flesh' and not 'soul', belittling human boastings. And why 'before Him' and not 'before men'? Because the boasting upon our own advantages was set in opposition to the boasting upon God. For what was necessary to write upon God, they were writing upon men. Therefore he said 'before Him'; for boasting occurring before Him, He who sees all, was impious. And that he said 'before Him' and not 'in the presence' is shown by this whole hypothesis; for those boast in words and in baptizing, and make the word about other things. 1 Cor 1:30

But of Him you are. All similarly say now that it has been said according to the being saved, not according to the logic of creation, as it is said elsewhere: those who were not born of blood nor of the will of the flesh, but of God. If therefore [it is] of Him, how shall we boast in our own advantages? But [it is] in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom and sanctification and redemption; not the wisdom of men saved—for it was wandering—but He Himself has become wisdom for us unto the knowledge of God; not the understanding of men snatched away, but Jesus having been crucified. Not men redeemed, so that the boasting may be from the Savior, not from the saved. 1 Cor 2:3–4 I was always afraid lest you be puffed up by outward training, since I did not use the persuasive wisdom. And in weakness, he says, the weakness from persecutions—for this is his custom to say everywhere—in weakness and in fear and in trembling, the weakness of those from whom I was persecuted. I demonstrated the fear and the trembling concerning you, I was all humble, so that you might be taught by this and not be puffed up. Since he said: 'my word, so that the opposite might not glory'.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The distinction of the Spirit and the unity of knowledge
english: Presenting this, which is eloquence, he says: my preaching is not in persuasive words of wisdom, because wisdom is not of words but of divine knowledge, of spirit and power. Since indeed the Holy Spirit provides the word of wisdom and also performs wonders, he said: in the demonstration of spirit and power; for that which is called not yet a demonstration, but the wonder possesses the demonstration.

He shows that he did not preach relying on any human ability; for he was in weakness and fear and trembling and in such things, as if he were in persecutions and afflictions. Because merely speaking, he did not overcome those using wisdom and trusting themselves in the word, but performing powers he showed the strength of God, and from there the preaching was well brought forth: but in the demonstration of spirit and power, so that your faith might not be in human wisdom but in the power of God.

This is not in things considered estimable, but in those perfect according to piety. And in the perfect, he says, not indeed to the perfect ones, for one speaks to those happening to be present and often receives many contradictions, but he who introduces the saving word to the perfect and pious does not speak as if depositing and treasuring the words in their souls.

If it was hidden, it is clear that it was not of calculations to find it, but truly it was of God to reveal it. And the demonstration of not knowing, instead of saying: for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. And he calls the ones concerning Pilate and Herod 'rulers', but the incarnate God 'the Lord of glory'.

This use is not carried out for these rhetoricians in the old way, but signifying the same with other words; for Isaiah says: Lord, who believed our hearing? and to whom was the arm of the Lord revealed? and who will recount his origin? and Moses: the secret things belong to the Lord our God. But the secret of God, clearly, both eye and heart he has pierced. One must not think, however, that God strictly revealed the mystery to some and allowed others to perish in ignorance, but it is necessary to know and be convinced that by his foreknowing power he provided to each, measuring according to merit, that which is for their benefit; for he foresees each.

The depths of God have spoken his deepest things, which have surpassed us in administration. Through these things he shows that he searches, not as one ignorant but as one who knows. Since some say the Spirit is the Father and others the Son, one must speak regarding each separately. It is impossible to say the Father; for he says we received not the spirit of the world but the spirit from God, and no one of it is [the Father]; for if it were spoken about God, from whom is God? As for the Son, it is possible to suppose him, but to be that about whom the Word is not possible; for who would say the God-Word searches so that he might learn the things of God? If they said the Son is being taught, how would he not have known from the following that just as the spirit in him knew things as a human spirit, so also the Spirit of God. Apart from this, the Holy Spirit is shown throughout the whole field. It should be noted that the Holy Spirit he says is from God, but the unclean one he did not say is from the world but is of the world; for the Paraclete is not a part of God, whereas the devil, according to having come to be, is a part of the creation. But the Holy Spirit is from God.

Not so that he might show, as the spirit in us is better than us, so also in God the spirit is better than him, immediately saying: for what man knows the things of the man except the spirit in him? But what is in God? For the one in him shows a part being the fullness of the man, but the one from him shows the cause. It should be noted that God and the Holy Spirit are two persons, but man and the spirit in him are not two persons but one man. Thus, showing the exact identity of the Father and the Spirit according to knowledge, he compared the knowledge of the spirit in us to the knowledge of the Father and the Spirit, so that it might be shown that in us, in the one and the same spirit, which is the soul and the mind, there is no discord of union; we know what we know, and so also in Father and Holy Spirit there is no discord of knowledge but identity. In order that we might know the things granted to us by God, the Spirit having given, the mind having grasped. And we speak. Again he shows another thing; not only says, not...
